# Results — Study 876 (Industry-Relative MAX)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — a refinement
of study 365 (Bali, Cakici & Whitelaw 2011, *"Maxing Out"*): sorting on a name's **maximum
daily return** (MAX) predicts lower future returns; here we sort on the **industry-relative**
MAX (own MAX minus the sector peers' median MAX) to isolate idiosyncratic lottery demand, and
ask whether it **sharpens** or **kills** the negative MAX→return relation. Offline &
deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of
**2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped).
Fingerprint `5384b8f7f128` (panel Close). Stamped as-of 2026-06-30.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily OHLC (`auto_adjust=True`, total-return), **50 liquid US large-caps**, 2010-01-04 → 2026-06-30, **4,147** dated rows/name |
| Universe | a fixed `UNIVERSE` of ~50 mega-caps, pulled through the **`quantlab.universe` survivorship guard** (`download_panel(..., allow_survivorship_bias=True)`), cached under this study's own `_cache/` |
| Sectors | each name tagged with its **GICS sector** (8 sectors: Info Tech, Financials, Industrials, Health Care, Consumer Discretionary, Consumer Staples, Communication Services, Energy) — the industry peer group |
| Signal | each name's monthly **MAX** = highest daily simple return over the calendar month (≥15 obs); **industry-relative MAX** = MAX − within-month **median MAX of the name's sector**, known at month-end |
| Sort | each month rank the cross-section by the signal into **quintiles**; **long Q1** (low MAX), **short Q5** (high MAX), equal-weight; earn each quintile's **next-month** return |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag: MAX at month-end `t` → hold month `t+1`. The costed timer charges 2 sides × one-way cost × NAV per monthly rebalance; the Q5 short book pays 50 bps/yr borrow |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC, `floor(4(n/100)^{2/9})`-lag) *t* on the monthly spread; one-sample *t*; a 20,000-draw sign-flip placebo; a two-era robustness cut; a 20-seed synthetic positive control |

**Survivorship — named on the Signal axis.** `UNIVERSE` is a **current-membership** list of
names that are liquid mega-caps *today*, so the magnitudes are an **upper bound**. Crucially,
the MAX / lottery premium is documented as a **small-and-illiquid-stock** effect; a 50-mega-cap
survivor panel is exactly where it is *least* likely to appear — which is what we find.

## The head-to-head — raw MAX vs industry-relative MAX

Monthly equal-weight **Q1 (low MAX) − Q5 (high MAX)** next-month spread (n = **197** months):

| sort | spread (bps/mo) | NW *t* | one-sample *t* | win-rate | gross Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **raw MAX** (study 365 style) | **−104.8** | **−2.42** | −2.53 | 43% | −0.62 |
| **industry-relative MAX** | **−89.7** | **−2.51** | −2.80 | 46% | −0.69 |

The claimed edge **fails to replicate — and inverts.** Bali-Cakici-Whitelaw predict a *positive*
long-low / short-high spread (dull low-MAX names out-earn the lottery tickets); on this mega-cap
universe **both** spreads are **significantly negative**: the lottery-like **high-MAX** names
actually *out-earned* the boring low-MAX ones over 2010–2026. The industry adjustment does **not
fix the sign**; it trims the magnitude (−104.8 → −89.7 bps) while nudging the *t* slightly more
extreme (−2.42 → −2.51) — a marginally cleaner knife on a claim that is not there. **A cleaner
measurement of the wrong-signed relation is not a rescue of the claim.**

## Quintile monotonicity — industry-relative MAX (annualised mean return)

| quintile | Q1 (low) | Q2 | Q3 | Q4 | Q5 (high) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| ann. mean | +17.5% | +13.1% | +15.5% | +17.0% | **+28.3%** |

Q5 (the high-MAX lottery names) posts the **highest** return — the sort runs backwards. These
are the momentum tech/discretionary mega-caps (NVDA, TSLA, AMD…) whose right tails paid off.

## Placebo — is the (reversed) relation a lucky alignment of the sort?

Sign-flip null on the industry-relative monthly spread (20,000 draws):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed spread | **−89.7 bps** |
| placebo mean (sd) | −0.19 bps (32.6) |
| position of observed | ≈ **2.75σ into the left tail** (right-tail p = 0.998 ⇒ left-tail p ≈ 0.002) |

The sign-flip null centres at zero; the observed −89.7 bps sits far in the **left** tail, so the
(opposite-sign) relation is real and not a lucky sort — the sign is simply the reverse of the
literature's on this universe.

## Robustness — two eras (split 2018-01-01)

| era | spread | NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 2010-01 → 2018-01 (n=96) | −47.1 bps | **−1.26** |
| 2018-01 → 2026-06 (n=101) | −130.2 bps | **−2.24** |

The wrong-sign relation is a **late-era phenomenon** — it is not significant in the first half
(*t* = −1.26). It therefore **fails the desk's sub-era robustness bar** even as a data-mined
reversal, reinforcing the None stamp.

## The timer — can you get paid for it?

Charge 2 sides × one-way × NAV per monthly rebalance on the long-short book; short pays 50
bps/yr borrow.

| one-way cost | gross/mo | cost/mo | net/mo | *t* (net) | ~ann. |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **1 bp** | −89.7 bps | 6.2 bps | **−95.9 bps** | −3.00 | −11.5%/yr |
| **5 bps** | −89.7 bps | 14.2 bps | **−103.9 bps** | −3.25 | −12.5%/yr |

The specified long-low / short-high book **loses money gross and net** at every cost. (Even the
data-mined *sign-flip* — long the lottery names — is a late-era-only artefact that fails the
robustness cut, so it is not an honest paycheck either.) **Mirage.**

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased AND the thesis holds

Deterministic seeded monthly panel where each name's MAX = an **un-priced sector-wide level** +
a **priced idiosyncratic pop** (`edge>0` depresses the high-idiosyncratic-MAX names' next-month
return). No network.

| world | raw-MAX NW *t* | industry-relative NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| null (`edge = 0`), **20 seeds** | — | mean **−0.25** (sd 0.88), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 1/20 seeds** |
| planted (`edge = 0.012`, seed 876) | **+11.18** | **+20.60** |

The detector recovers a *planted* MAX relation cleanly, never fires on the null beyond chance,
and — the study's thesis — the **industry adjustment sharpens** the planted effect (*t* +11.18 →
+20.60) by stripping the un-priced sector-wide MAX. So the negative real-tape result is a genuine
sign-reversal on the mega-cap universe, not a bug. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never
cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The industry-relative MAX does **not** sharpen a valid lottery effect on 50
  liquid US mega-caps, because the effect is **inverted** here: the Q1−Q5 spread is **−89.7
  bps/mo** (NW *t* = **−2.51**) — significant but *opposite in sign* to the claim (≈2.75σ into
  the left tail of a 20,000-draw placebo), and it holds **only in the late era** (*t* = −1.26
  early / −2.24 late). The industry adjustment barely moves the raw *t* (−2.42 → −2.51): a
  cleaner knife, no right-signed apple. A significant **wrong-sign** result fails the claim. The
  20-seed synthetic control recovers a *planted* relation and confirms the adjustment sharpens it
  (*t* +11.18 → +20.60), so the reversal is real, not machinery. Survivorship biases the
  magnitude (a small-cap effect probed on mega-caps).
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The specified long-low / short-high book loses money gross and net
  (−95.9 bps/mo at 1 bp, −103.9 at 5 bps); the data-mined sign-flip is a late-era-only artefact.
